subject: Direct vs Indirect damages — proposed negotiation language & approach
summary: Negotiation thread on carving out narrow direct economic loss remedies for data loss and lost margin while resisting broad lost-profits/goodwill claims. Legal recommended narrow, measurable carve-outs + escalation plan if counterparty insists on unlimited consequential claims.
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Need defensible MSA language: direct v indirect damages (FinClear)

Team — quick ask as I prep the FinClear negotiation later today. Their outside counsel pushed back hard on our limitation of liability and is insisting we remove a lot of our carve-outs for data-related losses. Key customer asks: full exclusion of "consequential/indirect damages" including lost profits and loss of goodwill, and an indemnity for data integrity incidents that would effectively create an unlimited exposure.

We want to hold firm on:
- A narrow carve-out for direct remediation costs for data loss/corruption (e.g., restore costs, reasonable third-party fees), and
- A narrowly capped remedy for lost gross margin (verified, short window) that is direct, not "consequential."

Can you please:
1) Draft 2 short redline alternatives we can send (one conservative/legal-first, one commercial compromise). Keep them measurable (restoration costs, 30-day lookback for lost margin, cap = greater of $X or 3x fees).
2) Flag any indemnity language we must avoid.
3) Suggest negotiation levers (insurance cert, SLA credits, higher cap, audit rights).

Attaching the current redline + a 1-pager with sample wording I pulled together. Need this before 2 PM PT so I can send to FinClear counsel.

—Marcus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
(attachment: FinClear_MSA_redline_v3.docx)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: contracts@finclear.com
Cc: samantha.rivera@finclear.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-01T13:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA — Limitation of Liability & damage categories (proposed text)

Andrew / FinClear team — following up with two alternate phrasing options for the damages section so we can close this line item. Attached full redline. Two short options below (Commercial / Legal). Please indicate which you prefer or propose edits in-line.

Option A — Commercial compromise (recommended):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, neither party will be liable for indirect, incidental, special, punitive or consequential damages, including lost profits and loss of business or goodwill, except that this limitation will not apply to: (i) damages arising from a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct; (ii) payment obligations; and (iii) direct, documented costs reasonably incurred to restore or recreate Customer Data ("Data Restoration Costs") and, to the extent directly caused by Redwood's breach of the Agreement, Customer's verified loss of gross margin for up to thirty (30) days following discovery, capped in the aggregate at the greater of $250,000 or three (3) times the fees paid by Customer to Redwood under the applicable Order Form in the prior twelve (12) months."

Option B — Legal-first (more protective):
"Except for payment obligations and claims arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, neither party will be liable for indirect, incidental, special, punitive or consequential damages, including lost profits, loss of data and loss of goodwill. For clarity, the foregoing does not limit a customer's right to recover documented out-of-pocket costs to remediate data corruption where such costs are direct and reasonable, subject to a cap equal to the greater of $100,000 or the fees paid in the prior 12 months."

Negotiation asks from our side: SLA credits + service credits, evidence of required cyber insurance; if you need a higher commercial cap we can consider 6x fees for enterprise customers with signed waiver.

Will await your counter.

—Marcus
(attachment: FinClear_MSA_redline_v3.docx)

From: Andrew Long <andrew.long@pearsonlaw.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, contracts@finclear.com
Cc: samantha.rivera@finclear.com
Date: 2026-09-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA — Limitation of Liability & damage categories (FinClear position)

Marcus / team — thanks for the quick options. FinClear's position is narrower than Option A: they want a clean, broad exclusion for indirect/consequential damages (including lost profits, loss of goodwill and business interruption) with no carve-out for lost profits and no cap carve-out that would re-introduce consequential recovery. They will, however, accept narrowly tailored first-party remediation costs for data restoration (reasonable third-party vendor fees and internal restoration labor) but only as a standalone limited exception and with a modest cap (they propose $50,000).

Two points to note from their side:
- They object to language that allows recovery of "lost gross margin" as they view it as inherently consequential and hard to verify.
- They require specific indemnity for breaches of data confidentiality which they say sits outside the limitation of liability and should be uncapped.

If Redwood insists on a lost-margin carve-out, they will need substantial commercial compensation (higher fees or tighter SLA).

Please propose final text or confirm you'll take this to execs for approval.

—Andrew
Pearson Law (outside counsel for FinClear)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-02T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Need defensible MSA language: direct v indirect damages (FinClear)

Marcus — quick read. Bottom-line analysis and recommended response: 

1) FinClear position summarized: broad exclusion for consequential/indirect (incl. lost profits/goodwill), willing to permit limited first‑party data remediation costs (cap ~$50k), wants uncapped data breach indemnity.

2) Legal risks/notes: 
- "Lost gross margin" is high-risk because courts often treat lost profits as consequential; narrow definitions and strict evidentiary limits are essential if we keep it.
- Uncapped indemnity for data breaches is a hard no unless it is tightly scoped (will require incident causation standard and carvebacks).

3) Negotiation playbook (recommended):
- Offer: Keep Option A commercial language but narrow the lost margin bucket: recovery limited to documented, verified lost margin for the lesser of 30 days or time reasonably required to restore, with a strict evidentiary standard (contemporaneous records, margin per SKU) and a cap at the greater of $150,000 or 2x fees.
- Trade: If FinClear insists on removing lost margin entirely, accept their $50k cap for Data Restoration Costs, but require (i) a mutual SLA credit schedule, and (ii) a representation of required cyber insurance (minimum limits) and (iii) a liability cap uplift (increase overall cap by a multiple) or price concession.
- Pushback on uncapped indemnity: propose language that: (i) limits indemnity to direct losses caused by a proven Redwood breach of its security obligations; (ii) requires notice and cure; (iii) limits recovery to demonstrable remediation costs and direct third-party claims (not speculative consequential damages).

4) Escalation: If FinClear won't budge, recommend we route to Director of Sales and Chief Legal Officer for final trade-offs (we should not uncap indemnity without exec sign-off).

I'll draft a redline with the middle-ground language and the fallback acceptance path. Sending in 90 minutes.

—Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: contracts@finclear.com
Cc: samantha.rivera@finclear.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-03T17:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA — Limitation of Liability & proposed final compromise

Andrew / FinClear team — appreciate the clarity. We've reviewed and propose a concise compromise we believe preserves commercial certainty while protecting both parties: 

Proposed compromise (final):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, neither party will be liable for indirect, incidental, special, punitive or consequential damages, including lost profits, loss of goodwill and business interruption, except for: (i) payment obligations; (ii) damages resulting from a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct; and (iii) direct, documented Data Restoration Costs (reasonable third‑party vendor fees and internal restoration labor) incurred to restore Customer Data, capped in the aggregate at the greater of $100,000 or the fees paid by Customer to Redwood under the applicable Order Form in the prior twelve (12) months. In addition, and only to the extent directly caused by Redwood's material breach of its security obligations under the Agreement, Customer may recover documented, verified loss of gross margin for a period not to exceed thirty (30) days following discovery, capped at $150,000; recovery under this clause requires contemporaneous documentation and an audit right for Redwood to validate calculation."

We will not agree to an uncapped general indemnity for data incidents; if FinClear requires an indemnity carveout it must be narrowly tied to proven Redwood-caused third-party claims and subject to the same caps and causation standards above.

If that is acceptable we can update the redline and route for signature. If you need a higher cap on the lost-margin carve-out, let us know what commercial trade you can offer (fee uplift or expanded SLA credits).

Thanks — Marcus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
